https://peps.python.org/pep-3134/.says: The rationale surveys earlier designs and describes Perl 6's RFC 88, whose mechanism keeps chained exceptions implicitly in an `@@` array, alongside precedents from Java, Ruby and C#.
https://peps.python.org/pep-3134/.quote: As for other languages, Java and Ruby both discard the original exception when another exception occurs in a `catch`/`rescue` or `finally`/`ensure` clause. Perl 5 lacks built-in structured exception handling. For Perl 6, RFC number 88 proposes an exception mechanism that implicitly retains chained exceptions in an array named `@@`. In that RFC, the most recently raised exception is exposed for matching, as in this PEP; also, arbitrary expressions (possibly involving `@@`) can be evaluated for exception matching.
https://peps.python.org/pep-3134/.rest: The next paragraph turns to C#, whose `InnerException` property is set explicitly through exception constructors rather than by the runtime.
